title: Harrow on the Hill Emergency Help Points
summary: Offline emergency medical, travel, and hazard information for Harrow on the Hill and HA1.
content:
For life-threatening emergencies, dial 999 or 112 immediately. During power cuts call 105; for gas leaks call 0800 111 999.

1. Nearest 24-Hour A&E Hospitals:
- Northwick Park Hospital: Watford Road, Harrow, HA1 3UJ. From Harrow-on-the-Hill station: ~25 min walk north-east along Peterborough Road and Sheepcote Road/Watford Road (~1.2 miles), or bus 182, 186, or 483 directly to hospital grounds.
- St Mary's Hospital (Major Trauma Centre): Praed Street, Paddington, W2 1NY. From Harrow-on-the-Hill station: ~10 miles south-east via Metropolitan line to central London or London bus services.
- St George's Hospital / North London Major Trauma Centre at Royal Free Hospital: Pond Street, NW3 2QG (~8 miles east).

2. Urgent Treatment Centres:
- Northwick Park Urgent Treatment Centre: Located at Northwick Park Hospital, Watford Road, Harrow, HA1 3UJ. Open 24/7 for treating urgent non-life-threatening illnesses and sprains/cuts.
- Alexandra Clinic (Urgent Care): Alexandra Avenue Health and Social Care Centre, 275 Alexandra Avenue, South Harrow, HA2 9DX. From Harrow-on-the-Hill station: ~35 min walk south-west (~1.8 miles), or bus 114 or 398.

3. Local Hazard Notes:
- Harrow on the Hill sits elevated above the Thames basin; however, low-lying ground at the foot of the hill (surrounding Roxborough Park, Roxeth, and streams connecting towards the River Brent system) experiences surface-water flash flooding during intense storms.
- Steep topography on the Hill itself can restrict vehicle movement during winter freeze or heavy runoff.

4. Essential Supplies:
Pharmacies and large food retailers along Station Road, College Road, and inside St Ann's / St George's shopping centres carry packaged water, first-aid items, and medication.

Note: addresses and opening hours may have changed — confirm on arrival where possible.
